candidate_changes: Skip sparse search when a full exact hit cannot be improved.
Require 64 additional reusable rows by default before automatically gathering a device sparse prefix.
Reject tiny actual gains even when request length allows a larger possible gain.
Check disabled/empty publication conditions before approximate session lookup.

method.warmup: One excluded source request per process.
method.producer: Frozen after warmup; measured branches cannot publish themselves.
method.driver_note: Final TQ driver additionally selects its required attention_kv_dtype at startup. Q8/exact config remains Q8; source warmup and measured call code are the same.

checks.device_manager_asan_ubsan: PASS; includes gains 1, 63, 64 and invalid zero; detect_leaks=0
checks.sparse_feature_after_policy: PASS; 761-row subset and 739-row prefix plus fresh suffix

conclusion: No material slowdown observed in these existing-path samples after dispatch fixes; not a proof of zero overhead or a statistically established speedup.
limitations: Single device and checkpoint; bounded 2048 context. No other SoC/platform or full CI matrix performance validation.
Device frequency and temperature not locked; sample ranges show drift. Differences of a few percent are not attributable speedups.
Enabled sparse search on sufficiently long misses/partial hits still scans candidate histories (about 6 microseconds on the pinned host fixture).
Metadata grows slightly. Unchanged KV payload does not imply identical total process memory or weight-page residency.
64-token gain is a conservative rule, not a universal cost model or guaranteed win for every sparse request.

host_metadata_layout_bytes.abi: x86-64 libstdc++; not an Android size claim
